closed_note: Closed with a date rather than overwritten, under Rule 7.3. Council approved a 3.75% Block 1 increase effective 1 January 2026; the 2026 observation opens when the updated statutory schedule is captured. Nothing here is recalculated when it is.
grade_reason: Grade C on the supply metric, and not because anything is missing. Toronto's statutory schedule is titled 'Water & Wastewater Consumption Rates' and prices a metered household with one per-cubic-metre figure covering both. There is no supply-only tariff to standardise. Total Water Services is a different matter: it is a clean function of volume, established from the by-law, with no recurring fixed charge and no ambiguity. The one open component, the tax treatment, closed on 19 August 2026 — by an enumerated bill rather than by a statutory provision, which is the same species of evidence that closed Abu Dhabi's recurring charge.

reference_connection.size: Metered residential service — no connection-size parameter
reference_connection.designation: Schedule 1 Ref 1 applies one rate to all metered consumers. Connection size appears in the code only in one-off installation fees, never in the consumption rate. Flat-rate and unmetered customers are priced per room and per fixture and are a different reference customer.

component_states.basis: Enumerated rather than assumed. Schedule 1 carries one per-cubic-metre figure for metered consumers, and every fee in Schedule 2 is a one-off event — installation, disconnection, meter test, turn-on, ownership change — or applies to flat-rate customers who refuse a meter. Nothing recurs on a metered household bill. Corroborated on 19 August 2026 by the City's live fee tables, which enumerate four schedules — utility bill, meter reading, water, wastewater — and contain nothing that recurs on a metered household account. The one standing charge on the page, the Flat Rate Legacy Fee, falls on an owner who has refused an automated meter and is therefore a different reference customer.
The instrument prices water and wastewater together and publishes no supply-only rate. This is a confirmed absence in the tariff, not an unanswered question.

Closed on 19 August 2026 by the City's own worked bill, not by a reading of the statute. The City computes a residential account at 38.50 m3, arrives at $187.22 of water/sewer charge and $111.20 of solid waste, and states the amount due as $298.42 — the sum of the two, with no tax line. The same page repeats the exercise for a bill paid late and closes the same way. A tax on the consumption charge would have to appear somewhere in that arithmetic and it does not. The rates page corroborates from the other side: it enumerates four fee tables and names HST three times, all three against Technical Review by Toronto Water staff, which is the same differential the statutory schedule shows, printed independently.
component_states.residual_caveat: The bill establishes that no tax is charged. It does not establish why. The record's earlier note that closing this needs the statutory provision was right about what a statute would add and wrong about what it would settle: the Excise Tax Act route for a combined water-and-wastewater charge is not obvious, since relief for unbottled water supplied by a municipality and relief for wastewater services are different questions with different answers. The provision stays in the queue as provenance. It is not holding a figure: what a household pays carries no tax, and that is now shown rather than inferred.

component_states.basis: Approximately five per cent off the water/sewer portion, stated exactly as 4.9981758%, lost if the bill is paid late. It is not modelled as a reduction: the City publishes two rates and this record uses the on-or-before figure, which is the after-due-date rate less the discount — 5.1188 x (1 - 0.049981758) = 4.86286. The discount and the two rates are one fact, and taking both would count it twice.

The City's live rates page prints $4.8629 per m3 on or before the due date and $5.1188 after, effective 1 January 2026. This record continues to publish the 2025 observation from the statutory schedule; the 2026 figure is recorded as observed so that rolling the observation forward is a decision somebody makes rather than a number that drifts in.

excluded.reason: A penalty differential of 5.26% for paying after the due date. §8 excludes penalties: the standardized household pays on time.
Applies to volume above 5,000 m³ a year of eligible industrial process use. Not a residential class.

excluded.item: Flat rate legacy fee, C$1,448.06 a year
excluded.reason: Charged to residential flat-rate consumers who refuse installation of an automatic meter. A penalty for refusal, and it applies to a customer class that is not metered.
Rule 3.1: means-tested, restricted to households consuming under 400 m³ a year, and describes a subset rather than a universal automatic feature.
Billed on the same City utility bill and are not part of receiving water. §8.
Toronto has no separate residential stormwater charge on the utility bill; where a city does, §8 excludes it from universal comparison.

refused_inferences.inference: Decomposing the combined rate at 43% water and 57% wastewater
refused_inferences.found_in: Schedule 3 Ref 2 prices a sewer surcharge on private water at 57% of the Block 1 rate
refused_inferences.arithmetic_it_would_give: C$2.0155/m³ supply and C$2.6717/m³ wastewater at the 2025 rate
refused_inferences.why_refused: The 57% is the rate charged to a customer who draws water privately and discharges to the sewer — a cost-recovery figure for that class. It is not a statement that the domestic rate divides in that proportion. Rule 3.3 leaves Water Supply empty rather than estimated, and a plausible ratio found in a neighbouring schedule is still an estimate.
refused_inferences.recorded_because: A later reader will find the same 57% and wonder why it was not used. The refusal is more useful written down than left to be rediscovered.

scope_disclosures: Reference account is a metered residential property. Flat-rate customers in the former City of Toronto are priced per room and per fixture and are a different reference customer.
The figure is a Total Water Services number. Toronto publishes no supply-only rate, so the TWJ Water Supply Bill does not exist for this city and is not estimated.
The 2025 rate. Council approved 3.75% from 1 January 2026 and this observation is closed at 31 December 2025.
shape_note: A flat combined rate with no fixed charge, so the effective price is the rate: the curve is flat and 15 m³ costs exactly fifteen times one cubic metre.

water_supply.blocked_by: Toronto publishes no supply-only rate. The statutory schedule prices water and wastewater together and Rule 3.3 leaves the supply figure empty rather than estimated.

total_water_services.basis: Established from Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 441, Schedule 1, a by-law. One per-cubic-metre rate, no recurring fixed charge confirmed by enumeration, no ambiguity. U = 0. Tax confirmed absent on 19 August 2026 from the City's own worked bill, which closes on the two service charges with no tax line.

total_water_services.reason: a combined figure cannot enter a supply-price index

jurisdiction.note: City is a display layer. The observation belongs to jurisdiction x utility x service area x customer class x schedule x period.

public_reconciliation.limits: Every case is computed at the 2026 rate, because that is the year the City's example uses. This record publishes the 2025 observation from the statutory schedule, so the reconciliation confirms the billing method and the absence of tax rather than the figure this record carries.

validation_note: Source verified, calculation verified, and reconciled at three lines against the City's own worked bill. The supply metric remains an exception: no arithmetic can split a rate the instrument does not divide.
